newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end higher on U.S. long bond fall.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end higher on U.S. long bond fall.

text.p: Argentine bonds ended higher Friday mostly on a U.S. long bond rate fall, but still in thin volume in a cautious market ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting Tuesday, dealers said.
The recovery was also helped by a strong liquidity of Argentine pension funds and higher Argentine ADRs and Brady Bond prices in New York, which recovered ground after two days of heavy losses.
The FRB was up 1-1/8 to 85-1/4. The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 gained $0.14 to 121.84.
"There are no fundamentals to justify the bonds price recovery," a dealer at a huge local bank said. "It was mainly due to the (U.S.) long bond rate decline."
Another trader agreed, saying, "There is a rebound, basically because of the long bond rate, but volume was thin."
The market was still cautious ahead of the Fed's meeting but most dealers think it won't change rates.
"December is a very seasonal month in the United States with Christmas sales and the Fed would hardly take it into account to make decisions on rates," the first dealer said.
